core_obligations: Identify the two cokernels: the proof recalls that the universal module of differentials is the cokernel of the displayed map and that the same holds on the pulled back sheaves of rings (proof lines 5107-5111)

Transport the free modules: it observes that the inverse image of the free module on the sets of sections of a sheaf of rings is the free module on the sets of sections of the inverse image, which it lists in the three cases appearing in the displayed map (proof lines 5111-5117)

Conclude: since the inverse image functor is exact, it commutes with cokernels, so the two constructions agree and the identification is compatible with the universal derivations (proof lines 5107-5118)

difficulty_reason: The counted statement identifies the inverse image of the universal module of differentials of a homomorphism of sheaves of rings with the universal module of differentials of the inverse images, compatibly with the universal derivations (author lemma at source lines 5095-5104, label lemma-pullback-differentials). The proof (source lines 5106-5118) uses that both modules are cokernels of the same kind of displayed map, that the inverse image functor is exact, and that it commutes with forming the free module on the sets of local sections, checking the three free modules appearing in the defining map (proof lines 5107-5117). The bookkeeping of the exactness and of the three free modules is the content; the defining map is reproduced as a context span. H2.
